title: Daniel Luis Martinez: The Blueprint | Exhibition
location: The Contemporary Art Museum of Indianapolis
description: Opening reception: Friday, October 2, 2026, 6–10pm  Exhibition on view: October 2–December 18, 2026  For this exhibition, the blueprint is used as both a representational and conceptual departure point. Daniel Luis Martinez uses cyanotype printmaking and mixed-media drawing techniques as a generative process to imagine a speculative home on the CAMi campus. The hybrid drawings and prints featured in the exhibition explore the tactile middle-ground of the blueprint as a creative endeavor.  The series employs orthographic conventions typical of architectural drawing sets, though not as precise instructions for building. Rather, a layered and loose approach expresses ideas of home as an architectonic language.  Daniel Luis Martinez is a registered architect, educator, and co-founder of the multi-disciplinary design studio LAA Office, which explores the intersection of landscape, art, and architecture. His research and creative work investigate the potential of public art to generate alternative forms of placemaking. Martinez is Associate Professor and Director of the IU Eskenazi School's J. Irwin Miller Architecture Program (https://architecture.indiana.edu/index.html) in Columbus, Indiana.  Learn more about the exhibition at the CAMI website (https://camindy.org/exhibitions-all/theblueprint).
source: IU Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design

title: In Search of Freedom: Stories of Afghanistan Exhibition
description: In Search of Freedom: Stories from Afghanistan  OPEN SEPTEMBER 4, 2026 - DECEMBER 4, 2026, MONDAY - FRIDAY 12-4 PM  OPEN 5-8 PM ON FIRST FRIDAYS OF THE MONTHIn Search of Freedom: Stories from Afghanistancelebrates the beauty, resilience, and rich cultural heritage of Afghanistan through an exhibition of oil paintings by Afghan artist Qahar Behzad, alongside the collaborative mural,August 15: A Mural for Afghanistan.Organized in partnership with Indiana University's Center for Refugee Studies and Exodus Refugee Immigration, the exhibition explores the humanity of the refugee experience through the lens of Afghanistan, inviting visitors to look beyond conflict and discover the stories and experiences of displaced people.The exhibition brings together Qahar's vibrant paintings - which honor Afghanistan's history, traditions, and everyday beauty - withAugust 15: A Mural for Afghanistan,a collaborative project led by Tiffany Black Behzad in collaboration with 59 Afghan evacuees at Camp Atterbury following the fall of Afghanistan to the Taliban on August 15, 2021. Developed through art therapy workshops with Afghan artists Zainab Ahmadi and Fawzia Abdaly, the mural preserves the participants' voices, memories, hopes, and resilience. The mural stands as a record of collective experience and a tribute to those who continue to seek safety, dignity, and freedom against all odds.Together, the artworks present a deeply human portrait of displacement, resilience, and belonging, inviting visitors to reflect on the the universal connections that unite us across borders, traditions, and generations, and the enduring human desire for freedom.
source: Architecture + Design, IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Eskenazi School of Art

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (https://go.iu.edu/america-250), a months-long civic festival offering our state expansive programming, exhibits, and events to honor our country's past while looking toward our shared future through common experiences for our campus and community.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers
description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence)  Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers—Philip Livingston of New York and James Smith of Pennsylvania—are on display in the North Gallery in The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment.
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Annie
location: Waldron Arts Center, 122 S Walnut St, Bloomington, IN 47404, USA
description:
Constellation Stage & Screen presents “Annie” on stage December 10th - January 3rd at the Waldron Auditorium.

Discover the magic of Annie, the iconic Broadway musical that has captured hearts for generations! The timeless tale of Little Orphan Annie follows a tenacious young girl whose unbreakable optimism leads her on an unforgettable journey from a New York City orphanage to a place she can finally call home. title: Daniel Luis Martinez: The Blueprint | Exhibition
location: The Contemporary Art Museum of Indianapolis
description: Opening reception: Friday, October 2, 2026, 6–10pm  Exhibition on view: October 2–December 18, 2026  For this exhibition, the blueprint is used as both a representational and conceptual departure point. Daniel Luis Martinez uses cyanotype printmaking and mixed-media drawing techniques as a generative process to imagine a speculative home on the CAMi campus. The hybrid drawings and prints featured in the exhibition explore the tactile middle-ground of the blueprint as a creative endeavor.  The series employs orthographic conventions typical of architectural drawing sets, though not as precise instructions for building. Rather, a layered and loose approach expresses ideas of home as an architectonic language.  Daniel Luis Martinez is a registered architect, educator, and co-founder of the multi-disciplinary design studio LAA Office, which explores the intersection of landscape, art, and architecture. His research and creative work investigate the potential of public art to generate alternative forms of placemaking. Martinez is Associate Professor and Director of the IU Eskenazi School's J. Irwin Miller Architecture Program (https://architecture.indiana.edu/index.html) in Columbus, Indiana.  Learn more about the exhibition at the CAMI website (https://camindy.org/exhibitions-all/theblueprint).
source: IU Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (https://go.iu.edu/america-250), a months-long civic festival offering our state expansive programming, exhibits, and events to honor our country's past while looking toward our shared future through common experiences for our campus and community.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers
description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence)  Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers—Philip Livingston of New York and James Smith of Pennsylvania—are on display in the North Gallery in The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment.

title: Preservation Hall Jazz Band: Creole Christmas
location: Buskirk-Chumley Theater, 114 East Kirkwood Avenue, Bloomington, IN 47408, USA
description:
Get in the holiday spirit with a New Orleans twist!

The Preservation Hall Jazz Band brings their beloved Creole Christmas to Bloomington! Join as the band performs New Orleans classics as well as some of our best-loved holiday selections with a twist.

The group derives its name from Preservation Hall, the venerable music venue located in the heart of New Orleans’ French Quarter, founded in 1961 by Allan and Sandra Jaffe. They’ve traveled worldwide spreading their mission to nurture and perpetuate the art form of New Orleans Jazz. Whether performing at Carnegie Hall or Lincoln Center, for British Royalty or the King of Thailand, this music embodies a joyful, timeless spirit. Under the auspices of current director, Ben Jaffe, the son of founders Allan and Sandra, Preservation Hall continues with a deep reverence and consciousness of its greatest attributes in the modern day as a venue, band, and record label.

The PHJB began touring in 1963 and for many years there were several bands successfully touring under the name Preservation Hall. Many of the band’s charter members performed with the pioneers who invented jazz in the early twentieth century including Buddy Bolden, Jelly Roll Morton, Louis Armstrong, and Bunk Johnson. Band leaders over the band’s history include the brothers Willie and Percy Humphrey, husband and wife Billie and De De Pierce, famed pianist Sweet Emma Barrett, and in the modern day Wendall and John Brunious. These founding artists and dozens of others passed on the lessons of their music to a younger generation who now follow in their footsteps like the current lineup.

The Playpen Sports Academy Curriculum is focused on a number of different goals including teaching children how to move and use their bodies, sharing with other children, interact in social settings, follow directions, and most importantly how to have fun in a physically active environment. At Playpen Sports Academy, we are focused as much on the individual development of your child as we are on sport specific skills that we teach. Because while we expect some of your children to go on to be great athletes, we expect all of your children to go on to be great people!

title: 2nd Weekend Work Day Trail Building
description:
Knobstone Hiking Trail Association of Indiana Meetup
Would you to spend a day in some beautiful woods with a delightful group of people building a connecting section of Indiana’s premier long distance hiking trail? Come join us as we continue work on the Tecumseh Trail extension portion of the KHT in MMSF. We will be building the new trail including clipping green briar.
Please bring a lunch and water. We will have large hand tools, but please bring any small tools you have such as clippers or a pruning saw. And a backpack is handy to carry everything in. Instructions will be provided for those who need them. We finish about 3:30.
Meet at the Hatfield Ridge Road parking lot. The gate is open. Go to the big sign on Rosenbaum/Catholic Cemetry Rd.
Join us on our website at http://www.knobstonehikingtrail.org/, on Facebook at [www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484](http://www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484), and Substack [https://khta.substack.com/](https://khta.substack.com/)

title: Nateland's Brian Bates Makes His Comedy Attic Debut!
location: The Comedy Attic, 123 S Walnut Street, Bloomington, IN
description: Comedian Brian Bates worked for nearly 20 years in corporate America until at the age of 43, he gave up his day job to pivot into a career as a stand-up comedian. Since then, the Nashville based comic has been touring the country performing at comedy clubs, theaters, corporate events, and churches. Brian has released two Dry Bar Comedy specials, titled Uber Important and Hello Folks . His latest special, titled Worried , was released in July 2026 on the Nateland Entertainment YouTube channel. As an originating member of the highly popular The Nateland Podcast , Brian served as a host and producer during the show’s six-year run. He now works with fellow comedians Aaron Weber and Dusty Slay as one of the hosts and producers of The Public Figures Podcast , heard by thousands of listeners each week. He performs regularly on the legendary Grand Ole Opry show and can be heard frequently on Pure Comedy Channel 98 on SiriusXM satellite radio. In addition to stand-up comedy, Brian made his acting debut appearing in two episodes of the 2022 Amazon sitcom Sprung . He most recently appeared in the 2026 Nate Bargatze movie The Breadwinner .

title: In Search of Freedom: Stories of Afghanistan Exhibition
description: In Search of Freedom: Stories from Afghanistan  OPEN SEPTEMBER 4, 2026 - DECEMBER 4, 2026, MONDAY - FRIDAY 12-4 PM  OPEN 5-8 PM ON FIRST FRIDAYS OF THE MONTHIn Search of Freedom: Stories from Afghanistancelebrates the beauty, resilience, and rich cultural heritage of Afghanistan through an exhibition of oil paintings by Afghan artist Qahar Behzad, alongside the collaborative mural,August 15: A Mural for Afghanistan.Organized in partnership with Indiana University's Center for Refugee Studies and Exodus Refugee Immigration, the exhibition explores the humanity of the refugee experience through the lens of Afghanistan, inviting visitors to look beyond conflict and discover the stories and experiences of displaced people.The exhibition brings together Qahar's vibrant paintings - which honor Afghanistan's history, traditions, and everyday beauty - withAugust 15: A Mural for Afghanistan,a collaborative project led by Tiffany Black Behzad in collaboration with 59 Afghan evacuees at Camp Atterbury following the fall of Afghanistan to the Taliban on August 15, 2021. Developed through art therapy workshops with Afghan artists Zainab Ahmadi and Fawzia Abdaly, the mural preserves the participants' voices, memories, hopes, and resilience. The mural stands as a record of collective experience and a tribute to those who continue to seek safety, dignity, and freedom against all odds.Together, the artworks present a deeply human portrait of displacement, resilience, and belonging, inviting visitors to reflect on the the universal connections that unite us across borders, traditions, and generations, and the enduring human desire for freedom.
source: Architecture + Design, IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Eskenazi School of Art

title: In Search of Freedom: Stories of Afghanistan Exhibition
description: In Search of Freedom: Stories from Afghanistan  OPEN SEPTEMBER 4, 2026 - DECEMBER 4, 2026, MONDAY - FRIDAY 12-4 PM  OPEN 5-8 PM ON FIRST FRIDAYS OF THE MONTHIn Search of Freedom: Stories from Afghanistancelebrates the beauty, resilience, and rich cultural heritage of Afghanistan through an exhibition of oil paintings by Afghan artist Qahar Behzad, alongside the collaborative mural,August 15: A Mural for Afghanistan.Organized in partnership with Indiana University's Center for Refugee Studies and Exodus Refugee Immigration, the exhibition explores the humanity of the refugee experience through the lens of Afghanistan, inviting visitors to look beyond conflict and discover the stories and experiences of displaced people.The exhibition brings together Qahar's vibrant paintings - which honor Afghanistan's history, traditions, and everyday beauty - withAugust 15: A Mural for Afghanistan,a collaborative project led by Tiffany Black Behzad in collaboration with 59 Afghan evacuees at Camp Atterbury following the fall of Afghanistan to the Taliban on August 15, 2021. Developed through art therapy workshops with Afghan artists Zainab Ahmadi and Fawzia Abdaly, the mural preserves the participants' voices, memories, hopes, and resilience. The mural stands as a record of collective experience and a tribute to those who continue to seek safety, dignity, and freedom against all odds.Together, the artworks present a deeply human portrait of displacement, resilience, and belonging, inviting visitors to reflect on the the universal connections that unite us across borders, traditions, and generations, and the enduring human desire for freedom.
source: Architecture + Design, IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Eskenazi School of Art

location: SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART
description: Looking for a welcoming space to crochet, knit, embroider, quilt, and explore other fiber arts? Interested in sharing your experiences and connecting with others while learning new skills? Or even just want a place to vent while you work on your scarf you've been crocheting for 2 years? Look no further; join us for Common Threads!  Common Threads is a free program open to the public and offers a welcoming environment to share, unwind, and learn! You can bring your own fiber art to work on while working alongside others who enjoy working in fiber and textiles. Or you can try learning something new; we welcome all skill levels! Either way, you're sure to have a good time.  This group meets on the 1st and 3rd Tuesday of each month from 3–4:30 p.m., excluding holidays and museum closures. The group will meet in the Roehm Family Art-making Studio, located inside the Simpson Center for Education on the 2nd floor of the Eskenazi Museum of Art.

title: Open Studio
location: SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART
description: Our Open Studio program invites participants to create in the museum's art studio, where art becomes a tool for reflection, expression, and connection. Guided by a trained art therapist, the open studio welcomes visitors to engage with materials at their own pace while drawing inspiration from the surrounding exhibitions. No art experience is needed; just bring your curiosity and a desire to create, and we'll handle the rest!  Participants are welcome to utilize supplies located in the studio, as well as bring their own supplies/projects to work on.  This group meets on the 2nd and 4th Wednesday of every month, excluding holidays and museum closures. It is open to everyone: students, staff, and the public included! The group will meet in the Roehm Family Art-making Studio, located inside the Simpson Center for Education on the 2nd floor of the Eskenazi Museum of Art.

title: Full Moon Hike, Brown County State Park
location: Brown County State Park, Olympic Pool parking lot, 1405 S.R. 46 W, Nashville, IN
description: Join a park naturalist for a guided night hike on the Salt Creek Trail! The Full Moon is the brightest night of the month, leading to interesting views along the creek. Learn about December's full moon this year, the Cold Moon. The Salt Creek Trail is rated very easy, but should be considered moderate in the dark. The trail has some minor slopes, a short stretch of lawn, and possible wet or icy spots depending on weather. Our route is  about 2 miles total and will take about an hour to complete. Please do not bring pets on night hikes. Red flashlights are preferred for night vision and can be loaned to hikers on request. Hike cancellation policy : Hikes will be cancelled if there is lightning, temperatures below 0 degrees Farenheit, temperature indexes above 105 degrees Farenheit, or a wind advisory. If a hike is cancelled, gatehouses will be informed. The phone number for the North Gatehouse is 812-988-5230.

title: Open Mic Night at The Comedy Attic
location: The Comedy Attic, 123 S Walnut St, Bloomington, IN 47408, USA
description:
Every Wednesday at 8PM is Comedy Attic Open Mic Night. Bloomington has one of the best local comedy scenes in the country, and it all starts with our open mic night!

Each comedian is asked to do no more than five minutes of completely original material. While we do not care about foul language in your set, we do not allow racist, homophobic, transphobic or rape/female bashing jokes. If you have to ask if it's racist, homophobic, transphobic or a rape joke, it probably is.

Comedians that wish to participate are asked to e-mail comedyattic@gmail.com mailto:comedyattic@gmail.com . Newcomers and any participants who are not paid professionals will be required to bring audience members to see them. This is non-negotiable. So if you plan on signing up, be sure to invite as many friends as you can. Good luck!

title: In Search of Freedom: Stories of Afghanistan Exhibition
description: In Search of Freedom: Stories from Afghanistan  OPEN SEPTEMBER 4, 2026 - DECEMBER 4, 2026, MONDAY - FRIDAY 12-4 PM  OPEN 5-8 PM ON FIRST FRIDAYS OF THE MONTHIn Search of Freedom: Stories from Afghanistancelebrates the beauty, resilience, and rich cultural heritage of Afghanistan through an exhibition of oil paintings by Afghan artist Qahar Behzad, alongside the collaborative mural,August 15: A Mural for Afghanistan.Organized in partnership with Indiana University's Center for Refugee Studies and Exodus Refugee Immigration, the exhibition explores the humanity of the refugee experience through the lens of Afghanistan, inviting visitors to look beyond conflict and discover the stories and experiences of displaced people.The exhibition brings together Qahar's vibrant paintings - which honor Afghanistan's history, traditions, and everyday beauty - withAugust 15: A Mural for Afghanistan,a collaborative project led by Tiffany Black Behzad in collaboration with 59 Afghan evacuees at Camp Atterbury following the fall of Afghanistan to the Taliban on August 15, 2021. Developed through art therapy workshops with Afghan artists Zainab Ahmadi and Fawzia Abdaly, the mural preserves the participants' voices, memories, hopes, and resilience. The mural stands as a record of collective experience and a tribute to those who continue to seek safety, dignity, and freedom against all odds.Together, the artworks present a deeply human portrait of displacement, resilience, and belonging, inviting visitors to reflect on the the universal connections that unite us across borders, traditions, and generations, and the enduring human desire for freedom.
source: Architecture + Design, IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Eskenazi School of Art

title: Toddler Sports Classes
description: Playpen Sports Academy is a wonderful way to introduce your child to the world of sport and physical activity in a non-intimidating environment with a small group of other toddlers and parents. The Playpen Sports Academy Curriculum is focused on a number of different goals including teaching children how to move and use their bodies, sharing with other children, interact in social settings, follow directions, and most importantly how to have fun in a physically active environment. At Playpen Sports Academy, we are focused as much on the individual development of your child as we are on sport specific skills that we teach. Because while we expect some of your children to go on to be great athletes, we expect all of your children to go on to be great people!

title: Annie

description:
Constellation Stage & Screen presents “Annie” on stage December 10th - January 3rd at the Waldron Auditorium.

Discover the magic of Annie, the iconic Broadway musical that has captured hearts for generations! The timeless tale of Little Orphan Annie follows a tenacious young girl whose unbreakable optimism leads her on an unforgettable journey from a New York City orphanage to a place she can finally call home. Featuring one of Broadway’s most memorable scores, including “It’s the Hard-Knock Life,” “Easy Street,” “N.Y.C.” and the endlessly-uplifting “Tomorrow,” Annie is a delightful theatrical experience for the entire family. Fun for all ages!

Open Dialogue: Share experiences and ask questions to gain valuable perspectives from fellow Dads who have walked a similar path.

Confidentiality: Safety is built when we can trust that what we share will remain with the people with whom we choose to share.

location: SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART
description: Our Open Studio program invites participants to create in the museum's art studio, where art becomes a tool for reflection, expression, and connection. Guided by a trained art therapist, the open studio welcomes visitors to engage with materials at their own pace while drawing inspiration from the surrounding exhibitions. No art experience is needed; just bring your curiosity and a desire to create, and we'll handle the rest!  Participants are welcome to utilize supplies located in the studio, as well as bring their own supplies/projects to work on.  This group meets on the 2nd and 4th Wednesday of every month, excluding holidays and museum closures. It is open to everyone: students, staff, and the public included! The group will meet in the Roehm Family Art-making Studio, located inside the Simpson Center for Education on the 2nd floor of the Eskenazi Museum of Art.

title: Open Mic Night at The Comedy Attic
location: The Comedy Attic, 123 S Walnut St, Bloomington, IN 47408, USA
description:
Every Wednesday at 8PM is Comedy Attic Open Mic Night. Bloomington has one of the best local comedy scenes in the country, and it all starts with our open mic night!

Each comedian is asked to do no more than five minutes of completely original material. While we do not care about foul language in your set, we do not allow racist, homophobic, transphobic or rape/female bashing jokes. If you have to ask if it's racist, homophobic, transphobic or a rape joke, it probably is.

Comedians that wish to participate are asked to e-mail comedyattic@gmail.com mailto:comedyattic@gmail.com . Newcomers and any participants who are not paid professionals will be required to bring audience members to see them. This is non-negotiable. So if you plan on signing up, be sure to invite as many friends as you can. Good luck!

title: New Year's Eve Starring Brent Terhune!
location: The Comedy Attic, 123 S Walnut Street, Bloomington, IN
description: Spend the biggest night in comedy at one the top 5 comedy clubs in the country! 10:30 show includes a champagne toast as we count down to 2027! Brent Terhune is a nationally-touring stand-up comedian, writer, and podcaster. His comedy album, Mr. Turkey, went to #1 on iTunes. Brent got his start in stand-up comedy in Indianapolis, Indiana at the age of 16. Most people would describe him as a white man, but according to Brent he “got the black knocked off of him at an early age when he refused to clean up his room” and he is now doomed to walk the earth as a pale redhead or as he likes to call himself a real “OG” or Original Ginger. Not many comics can pull off Brent’s laid-back style of comedy and still remain just as absurd, relevant, and funny as he is. Whether talking about the everyday struggles of being a redhead, life as a college student and radio DJ, or his off-the-wall Uncle Frank and family, Brent is sure to keep you laughing well after he’s left the stage. Characters, voices, one liners, and time-tested monologues - Brent Terhune is the embodiment of all these things and more. Currently, Brent is a writer for the nationally syndicated Bob & Tom Radio Show (he’s been on the show, too) as well as the co-host of the immensely popular podcast that is enjoyed by dozens of listeners, The Interweb Podshow. He’s the creator, writer, and illustrator of the Uncle Frank comic strip and he’s performed at the Iowa Comedy Festival, Gilda’s Laugh Fest, and the Cleveland Comedy Festival (runner up 2012), the Limestone Comedy Festival, and the Laugh Your Ashville Off Comedy Festival.

description: Playpen Sports Academy is a wonderful way to introduce your child to the world of sport and physical activity in a non-intimidating environment with a small group of other toddlers and parents. At Playpen Sports Academy, we are focused as much on the individual development of your child as we are on sport specific skills that we teach. Because while we expect some of your children to go on to be great athletes, we expect all of your children to go on to be great people!

description:
Constellation Stage & Screen presents “Annie” on stage December 10th - January 3rd at the Waldron Auditorium.

Discover the magic of Annie, the iconic Broadway musical that has captured hearts for generations! The timeless tale of Little Orphan Annie follows a tenacious young girl whose unbreakable optimism leads her on an unforgettable journey from a New York City orphanage to a place she can finally call home. Featuring one of Broadway’s most memorable scores, including “It’s the Hard-Knock Life,” “Easy Street,” “N.Y.C.” and the endlessly-uplifting “Tomorrow,” Annie is a delightful theatrical experience for the entire family. Fun for all ages!

See Constellation’s website for more information, including a detailed performance schedule. Learn more and find tickets at seeconstellation.org/kids/annie/ https://seeconstellation.org/kids/annie/

The Community Bike Project is a Bloomington-based organization that focuses on providing bike transportation to the people of the city. We focus on teaching bicycle maintenence in order to ensure that bikes on the streets stay on the streets. Here is what we do: Community Bike Project Front Door



    * bikes for sale: we sell gently used bikes at bargain prices

    * advocacy: we support alternative forms of transportation; we support the reuse and recycling of bicycles

    * workshops & classes: we offer unique bike maintence workshops and classes for children and adults

    * open shop: we make our tools available to the public

Open Mic Night at The Comedy Attic
location: The Comedy Attic, 123 S Walnut St, Bloomington, IN 47408, USA
description:
Every Wednesday at 8PM is Comedy Attic Open Mic Night. Bloomington has one of the best local comedy scenes in the country, and it all starts with our open mic night!

Each comedian is asked to do no more than five minutes of completely original material. While we do not care about foul language in your set, we do not allow racist, homophobic, transphobic or rape/female bashing jokes. If you have to ask if it's racist, homophobic, transphobic or a rape joke, it probably is.

Comedians that wish to participate are asked to e-mail comedyattic@gmail.com mailto:comedyattic@gmail.com . Newcomers and any participants who are not paid professionals will be required to bring audience members to see them. This is non-negotiable. So if you plan on signing up, be sure to invite as many friends as you can. Good luck!

Free to play and open to teams of any size, this lively weekly event is perfect for both serious trivia buffs and casual players looking for a fun midweek outing. Prizes are awarded to the top teams, and Moontown’s relaxed atmosphere, local brews, and great food make it an ideal spot to unwind and connect with friends in Brown County. Trivia takes place Wednesdays from 6–8 PM.

title: Toddler Sports Classes
description: Playpen Sports Academy is a wonderful way to introduce your child to the world of sport and physical activity in a non-intimidating environment with a small group of other toddlers and parents. The Playpen Sports Academy Curriculum is focused on a number of different goals including teaching children how to move and use their bodies, sharing with other children, interact in social settings, follow directions, and most importantly how to have fun in a physically active environment. At Playpen Sports Academy, we are focused as much on the individual development of your child as we are on sport specific skills that we teach. Because while we expect some of your children to go on to be great athletes, we expect all of your children to go on to be great people!

title: 2nd Weekend Work Day Trail Building
description:
Knobstone Hiking Trail Association of Indiana Meetup
Would you like to spend a day in some beautiful woods with a delightful group of people building a connecting section of Indiana’s premier long distance hiking trail? Come join us as we continue work on the Tecumseh Trail extension portion of the KHT in MMSF. We will be building the new trail including clipping green briar.
Please bring a lunch and water. We will have large hand tools, but please bring any small tools you have such as clippers or a pruning saw. And a backpack is handy to carry everything in. Instructions will be provided for those who need them. We finish about 3:30.
Meet at the parking lot at the base of Gose Creek Road at the end of Hinson Road in Martinsville.
Join us on our website at http://www.knobstonehikingtrail.org/, on Facebook at [www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484](http://www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484), and Substack [https://khta.substack.com/](https://khta.substack.com/)

title: Daughters of the King - Meeting
description: Daughters of the King “DOK” is a world-wide religious order founded in 1885 by Episcopal women. Today it includes women from a wide variety of Christian traditions. Members of the DOK are ordinary women who are married and single, live in the world, and dedicate themselves prayer, service and evangelism. Monthly gatherings include educational programs; recent programs at Trinity have highlighted Amish communities of faith, virtual prayer retreats, handling conflict, book reviews, the Lenten season, Mary Magdalene, and many other topics related to Christian faith and life. Members help with church events throughout the year.Trinity’s chapter usually meets on the 2nd Monday of the month at 5:00 pm in the Church Library; check the announcements in the Sunday worship bulletin for any change in location. All women interested in loving service and spiritual fellowship are welcome. For more information contact the Rev. Virginia Hall at yesvirginia1942@gmail.com or Heather Lake at hr42lake@gmail.com.

title: Mathematics as a Medium | Exhibition
location: Fine Arts Building, 1201 East 7th Street, Bloomington, IN 47405
description: Exhibition Opening Reception: January 15, 6:30–8:30 pmExhibition Dates: January 15–March 6Symposium Dates: January 15–16  Curated by Associate Professor of Interior Design in the Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design Jiangmei Wu, the exhibition "Mathematics as a Medium" opening Friday, January 15 at Indiana University's Grunwald Gallery of Art complements a symposium January 15 and 16 convening many of the exhibitors with counterparts from across the international mathematical art community. Over three keynotes, thematic panels, and workshops, participating artists, designers, mathematicians, and scholars will explore mathematics as an active medium of creative practice and create a shared space for exchange among disciplines.  The coordinated events seek to usher in a broader understanding of the relationship between mathematics and art. Proceeding from the proposition that mathematics is a mediumsuch as paint, stone, or sound—through which artists and designers create and cultures express themselves, the exhibition and symposium are designed more broadly to redefine mathematics as a living, generative practice that shapes how we think, make, and experience the world.Visit here for more information about the exhibition. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/exhibitions/grunwald-gallery/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium.html)Visit here for the symposium schedule. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/events/special-events/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium-symposium.html)This project was supported by Indiana University's Presidential Arts and Humanities Program; the Office for Research Development, Indiana University Research; and also at Indiana University Bloomington: Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design; Department of Mathematics; and Luddy School of Informatics, Computing and Engineering Artificial Intelligence Center (LAIC).
source: IU Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design

title: Lecture: A Failure of Will: Why Cyber Operations Against Ukraine's and Poland's Energy Systems Go Unanswered with Szymon Skalski
description: Cyber operations against power grids and heating systems recur in war and outside it. The same conduct falls under the law of armed conflict in one setting, peacetime international law in the other. Drawing on Russian operations in Ukraine and Poland, this lecture asks why correct legal classification so rarely brings consequences.  Szymon Skalski is a doctoral candidate at Jagiellonian University and Visiting Scholar at IU's Ostrom Workshop, where he leads its working group on environmental security and technological risk in conflict. His research interests include cybersecurity of critical infrastructure, global security, and liability for cyberattacks.

title: An Evening With Phil Hanley
location: The Comedy Attic, 123 S Walnut Street, Bloomington, IN
description: Originally from Oshawa, Canada, Phil is now a key figure in the NYC comedy scene, performing regularly at the Comedy Cellar. With nearly 650K followers on Instagram and nearly 400K followers and 15.6 million likes on TikTok, he’s appeared on major late-night shows like The Tonight Show , Late Night with Seth Meyers , and The Late Late Show . Hanley’s memoir, SPELLBOUND: My Life as a Dyslexic , chronicles his lifelong struggle with dyslexia and how comedy became his saving grace. Hanley’s goal in writing this book is to continue his advocacy for dyslexia awareness and his commitment to using his platform to inspire others and promote a deeper understanding of neurodiversity. He also self-released his stand-up special, Ooh La La , on YouTube (where he has nearly 675k followers), which has amassed over 2 million views . Additionally, Phil was featured in the film I Feel Pretty and the Comedy Central series Inside Amy Schumer , with his half-hour special available on Comedy Central and iTunes. His 2018 album, Please Don’t Chit Chat While I’m Pursuing My Dream , is a fan favorite.

description: Playpen Sports Academy is a wonderful way to introduce your child to the world of sport and physical activity in a non-intimidating environment with a small group of other toddlers and parents. title: 2nd Weekend Work Day Trail Building
description:
Knobstone Hiking Trail Association of Indiana Meetup
Would you to spend a day in some beautiful woods with a delightful group of people building a connecting section of Indiana’s premier long distance hiking trail? Come join us as we continue work on the Tecumseh Trail extension portion of the KHT in MMSF. We will be building the new trail including clipping green briar.
Please bring a lunch and water. We will have large hand tools, but please bring any small tools you have such as clippers or a pruning saw. And a backpack is handy to carry everything in. Instructions will be provided for those who need them. We finish about 3:30.
Meet at the Hatfield Ridge Road parking lot. The gate is open. Go to the big sign on Rosenbaum/Catholic Cemetry Rd.
Join us on our website at http://www.knobstonehikingtrail.org/, on Facebook at [www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484](http://www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484), and Substack [https://khta.substack.com/](https://khta.substack.com/)

title: An Evening With Phil Hanley
location: The Comedy Attic, 123 S Walnut Street, Bloomington, IN
description: Originally from Oshawa, Canada, Phil is now a key figure in the NYC comedy scene, performing regularly at the Comedy Cellar. With nearly 650K followers on Instagram and nearly 400K followers and 15.6 million likes on TikTok, he’s appeared on major late-night shows like The Tonight Show , Late Night with Seth Meyers , and The Late Late Show . Hanley’s memoir, SPELLBOUND: My Life as a Dyslexic , chronicles his lifelong struggle with dyslexia and how comedy became his saving grace. Hanley’s goal in writing this book is to continue his advocacy for dyslexia awareness and his commitment to using his platform to inspire others and promote a deeper understanding of neurodiversity. He also self-released his stand-up special, Ooh La La , on YouTube (where he has nearly 675k followers), which has amassed over 2 million views . Additionally, Phil was featured in the film I Feel Pretty and the Comedy Central series Inside Amy Schumer , with his half-hour special available on Comedy Central and iTunes. His 2018 album, Please Don’t Chit Chat While I’m Pursuing My Dream , is a fan favorite.

title: Mathematics as a Medium | Exhibition
location: Fine Arts Building, 1201 East 7th Street, Bloomington, IN 47405
description: Exhibition Opening Reception: January 15, 6:30–8:30 pmExhibition Dates: January 15–March 6Symposium Dates: January 15–16  Curated by Associate Professor of Interior Design in the Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design Jiangmei Wu, the exhibition "Mathematics as a Medium" opening Friday, January 15 at Indiana University's Grunwald Gallery of Art complements a symposium January 15 and 16 convening many of the exhibitors with counterparts from across the international mathematical art community. Over three keynotes, thematic panels, and workshops, participating artists, designers, mathematicians, and scholars will explore mathematics as an active medium of creative practice and create a shared space for exchange among disciplines.  The coordinated events seek to usher in a broader understanding of the relationship between mathematics and art. Proceeding from the proposition that mathematics is a mediumsuch as paint, stone, or sound—through which artists and designers create and cultures express themselves, the exhibition and symposium are designed more broadly to redefine mathematics as a living, generative practice that shapes how we think, make, and experience the world.Visit here for more information about the exhibition. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/exhibitions/grunwald-gallery/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium.html)Visit here for the symposium schedule. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/events/special-events/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium-symposium.html)This project was supported by Indiana University's Presidential Arts and Humanities Program; the Office for Research Development, Indiana University Research; and also at Indiana University Bloomington: Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design; Department of Mathematics; and Luddy School of Informatics, Computing and Engineering Artificial Intelligence Center (LAIC).

location: The Comedy Attic, 123 S Walnut St, Bloomington, IN 47408, USA
description:
Every Wednesday at 8PM is Comedy Attic Open Mic Night. Bloomington has one of the best local comedy scenes in the country, and it all starts with our open mic night!

Each comedian is asked to do no more than five minutes of completely original material. While we do not care about foul language in your set, we do not allow racist, homophobic, transphobic or rape/female bashing jokes. If you have to ask if it's racist, homophobic, transphobic or a rape joke, it probably is.

Comedians that wish to participate are asked to e-mail comedyattic@gmail.com mailto:comedyattic@gmail.com . Newcomers and any participants who are not paid professionals will be required to bring audience members to see them. This is non-negotiable. So if you plan on signing up, be sure to invite as many friends as you can. Good luck!

title: Mathematics as a Medium | Exhibition
location: Fine Arts Building, 1201 East 7th Street, Bloomington, IN 47405
description: Exhibition Opening Reception: January 15, 6:30–8:30 pmExhibition Dates: January 15–March 6Symposium Dates: January 15–16  Curated by Associate Professor of Interior Design in the Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design Jiangmei Wu, the exhibition "Mathematics as a Medium" opening Friday, January 15 at Indiana University's Grunwald Gallery of Art complements a symposium January 15 and 16 convening many of the exhibitors with counterparts from across the international mathematical art community. Over three keynotes, thematic panels, and workshops, participating artists, designers, mathematicians, and scholars will explore mathematics as an active medium of creative practice and create a shared space for exchange among disciplines.  The coordinated events seek to usher in a broader understanding of the relationship between mathematics and art. Proceeding from the proposition that mathematics is a mediumsuch as paint, stone, or sound—through which artists and designers create and cultures express themselves, the exhibition and symposium are designed more broadly to redefine mathematics as a living, generative practice that shapes how we think, make, and experience the world.Visit here for more information about the exhibition. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/exhibitions/grunwald-gallery/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium.html)Visit here for the symposium schedule. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/events/special-events/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium-symposium.html)This project was supported by Indiana University's Presidential Arts and Humanities Program; the Office for Research Development, Indiana University Research; and also at Indiana University Bloomington: Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design; Department of Mathematics; and Luddy School of Informatics, Computing and Engineering Artificial Intelligence Center (LAIC).
source: IU Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design

title: Mathematics as a Medium | Exhibition
location: Fine Arts Building, 1201 East 7th Street, Bloomington, IN 47405
description: Exhibition Opening Reception: January 15, 6:30–8:30 pmExhibition Dates: January 15–March 6Symposium Dates: January 15–16  Curated by Associate Professor of Interior Design in the Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design Jiangmei Wu, the exhibition "Mathematics as a Medium" opening Friday, January 15 at Indiana University's Grunwald Gallery of Art complements a symposium January 15 and 16 convening many of the exhibitors with counterparts from across the international mathematical art community. Over three keynotes, thematic panels, and workshops, participating artists, designers, mathematicians, and scholars will explore mathematics as an active medium of creative practice and create a shared space for exchange among disciplines.  The coordinated events seek to usher in a broader understanding of the relationship between mathematics and art. Proceeding from the proposition that mathematics is a mediumsuch as paint, stone, or sound—through which artists and designers create and cultures express themselves, the exhibition and symposium are designed more broadly to redefine mathematics as a living, generative practice that shapes how we think, make, and experience the world.Visit here for more information about the exhibition. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/exhibitions/grunwald-gallery/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium.html)Visit here for the symposium schedule. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/events/special-events/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium-symposium.html)This project was supported by Indiana University's Presidential Arts and Humanities Program; the Office for Research Development, Indiana University Research; and also at Indiana University Bloomington: Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design; Department of Mathematics; and Luddy School of Informatics, Computing and Engineering Artificial Intelligence Center (LAIC).
source: IU Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design

description: Playpen Sports Academy is a wonderful way to introduce your child to the world of sport and physical activity in a non-intimidating environment with a small group of other toddlers and parents. title: Rare Earth
description:
Celebrating 55 years of the iconic hit “I Just Want To Celebrate,” Motown’s token rock band Rare Earth will make a stop at the Brown County Music Center in Nashville, Ind., on Saturday, January 23, 2027.
Hailing from Detroit, Rare Earth were a band inspired by the Motor City’s twin legacies in hard rock and soul. Their biggest hits saw them covering classic songs of the past, while their sound found a middle ground between full-bodied rhythm & blues and tough bar band rock & roll. The band began in 1960 as the Sunliners and played in and around Detroit. In 1968 the group changed its name to one more reflective of the psychedelic age. Their tight musicianship found room for them to transform their songs through extended jams, with their biggest hit, “Get Ready,” often clocking in at 30 minutes in concert. Other hits included Temptations cover “(I Know) I’m Losing You,” original hit single, “Born to Wander,” and iconic signature song, “I Just Want To Celebrate.”

title: Mathematics as a Medium | Exhibition
location: Fine Arts Building, 1201 East 7th Street, Bloomington, IN 47405
description: Exhibition Opening Reception: January 15, 6:30–8:30 pmExhibition Dates: January 15–March 6Symposium Dates: January 15–16  Curated by Associate Professor of Interior Design in the Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design Jiangmei Wu, the exhibition "Mathematics as a Medium" opening Friday, January 15 at Indiana University's Grunwald Gallery of Art complements a symposium January 15 and 16 convening many of the exhibitors with counterparts from across the international mathematical art community. Over three keynotes, thematic panels, and workshops, participating artists, designers, mathematicians, and scholars will explore mathematics as an active medium of creative practice and create a shared space for exchange among disciplines.  The coordinated events seek to usher in a broader understanding of the relationship between mathematics and art. Proceeding from the proposition that mathematics is a mediumsuch as paint, stone, or sound—through which artists and designers create and cultures express themselves, the exhibition and symposium are designed more broadly to redefine mathematics as a living, generative practice that shapes how we think, make, and experience the world.Visit here for more information about the exhibition. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/exhibitions/grunwald-gallery/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium.html)Visit here for the symposium schedule. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/events/special-events/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium-symposium.html)This project was supported by Indiana University's Presidential Arts and Humanities Program; the Office for Research Development, Indiana University Research; and also at Indiana University Bloomington: Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design; Department of Mathematics; and Luddy School of Informatics, Computing and Engineering Artificial Intelligence Center (LAIC).
source: IU Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design

title: Open Mic Night at The Comedy Attic
location: The Comedy Attic, 123 S Walnut St, Bloomington, IN 47408, USA
description:
Every Wednesday at 8PM is Comedy Attic Open Mic Night. Bloomington has one of the best local comedy scenes in the country, and it all starts with our open mic night!

Each comedian is asked to do no more than five minutes of completely original material. While we do not care about foul language in your set, we do not allow racist, homophobic, transphobic or rape/female bashing jokes. If you have to ask if it's racist, homophobic, transphobic or a rape joke, it probably is.

Comedians that wish to participate are asked to e-mail comedyattic@gmail.com mailto:comedyattic@gmail.com . Newcomers and any participants who are not paid professionals will be required to bring audience members to see them. This is non-negotiable. So if you plan on signing up, be sure to invite as many friends as you can. Good luck!

title: Mathematics as a Medium | Exhibition
location: Fine Arts Building, 1201 East 7th Street, Bloomington, IN 47405
description: Exhibition Opening Reception: January 15, 6:30–8:30 pmExhibition Dates: January 15–March 6Symposium Dates: January 15–16  Curated by Associate Professor of Interior Design in the Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design Jiangmei Wu, the exhibition "Mathematics as a Medium" opening Friday, January 15 at Indiana University's Grunwald Gallery of Art complements a symposium January 15 and 16 convening many of the exhibitors with counterparts from across the international mathematical art community. Over three keynotes, thematic panels, and workshops, participating artists, designers, mathematicians, and scholars will explore mathematics as an active medium of creative practice and create a shared space for exchange among disciplines.  The coordinated events seek to usher in a broader understanding of the relationship between mathematics and art. Proceeding from the proposition that mathematics is a mediumsuch as paint, stone, or sound—through which artists and designers create and cultures express themselves, the exhibition and symposium are designed more broadly to redefine mathematics as a living, generative practice that shapes how we think, make, and experience the world.Visit here for more information about the exhibition. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/exhibitions/grunwald-gallery/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium.html)Visit here for the symposium schedule. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/events/special-events/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium-symposium.html)This project was supported by Indiana University's Presidential Arts and Humanities Program; the Office for Research Development, Indiana University Research; and also at Indiana University Bloomington: Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design; Department of Mathematics; and Luddy School of Informatics, Computing and Engineering Artificial Intelligence Center (LAIC).
source: IU Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design

title: IKS Colloquium - Junyoung Verónica Kim
description: IKS Spring 2027 Colloquium Series  Junyoung Verónica Kim  Department of Asian and Asian American Studies  Binghamton University  Gwangju from Buenos Aires: Missing Bodies and Forgotten Geographies in Im Heung-soon's Good Light, Good Air Friday, January 2912:00-1:00pmGISB 2067 | 355 N Eagleson Ave  On April 30th, 1977, fourteen mothers sent a letter asking the military dictator Jorge Rafael Videla for the whereabouts of their disappeared children and began to gather in silent protest in the Plaza de Mayo, Buenos Aires. Known as the Mothers of Plaza de Mayo, they spurred a mass movement that continues today. Around the same time, on May 18th, 1980, citizens of Gwangju, South Korea, launched a mass resistance movement against the dictatorship of Chun Doo-hwan. The South Korean military retaliated in full force resulting in the massacre and disappearance of thousands of Gwangju citizens. The connections and intimacies between the overlapping histories of these two cities demonstrate the ways in which Global South countries were violently conscripted into dirty wars against communism. Despite the explicit linkages, why are the histories of these two places (cities and nations) studied separately––divided by discrete disciplinary boundaries? How does insurgent memory both disrupt dominant historical national narratives and yoke together these two geographies/histories/futurities? Moreover, how does the present absence of the missing in Gwangju and the desaparecidos (disappeared) in Buenos Aires haunt the urban geographies that are shaped through the ordinary violence of gentrification and urban development? Through a reading of Im Heung-soon's video installation and documentary Good Light, Good Air (2018, 2020), Junyoung Verónica Kim explores the multiple vectors and scales of transpacific connectivity. Examined through Eyal Weizman's conceptualization of forensic architecture, the ruins, holes, and missing parts of both the material (bodies and urban geographies) and the epistemic (archives, knowledge production, disciplinary formation) testify to what cannot be visiblized or seen otherwise. In situating the Gwangju Uprising and the Argentine dirty war as part and parcel of the diasporic, this talk proposes that paying attention to Korean-Latin American intimacies offers a possibility of fabulating a decolonial and demilitarized world.   Open to the public. A light lunch will be served.

title: Pam Tillis & Lorrie Morgan
description:
Pam Tillis and Lorrie Morgan are currently delighting old and new fans across North America on their highly successful Grits and Glamour Tour. Veteran recording artists and performers, they grace the country format with style, flair, and undeniable talent that is captivating and timeless, and will make a stop at the Brown County Music Center in Nashville, Ind.
Formed in 2009, the Grits and Glamour tour is a “together is better” event. The show is only loosely scripted. Good-natured ribbing and off-the-cuff remarks are just part of the fun. They add tight harmonies to each other’s material, classic songs like Tillis’ “Maybe It Was Memphis,” and “Mi Vida Loca,” and Morgan’s “Something In Red” and “Except for Monday” as well as new and original music from more recent recordings. The ladies are backed by some of Nashville’s finest musicians and singers.
Their career highlights are numerous and varied. Combined, they have recorded 28 top 10 hits, more than 18 million records sold, and 12 number one songs. There have been Grammys, CMA Awards, movie credits, television appearances, and Broadway performances. They have rocked arenas, helmed world-class symphonies, and toured on almost every continent. These 50- somethings are more than a little flattered that they can still sell out shows, turn heads, and make hearts beat fast nearly four decades into their careers. It’s almost unnecessary to point out how rare it is to have such long-term success in an industry so fickle, but Pam Tillis and Lorrie Morgan haven’t missed a beat. In fact, they both maintain extensive solo touring schedules, enhanced by the buzz that surrounds the Grits and Glamour tour.

title: Hidden Mythologies: Altai Traditions & Myths
location: IU Museum of Archaeology and Anthropology, 416 N. Indiana Ave., Bloomington, IN 47408
description: Event Details:  Now in its second year, the Hidden Mythologieslecture series explores the rich and often overlooked mythological traditions of the peoples of the Volga-Ural region and beyond. Through stories of gods, spirits, legendary heroes, sacred landscapes, and traditional beliefs, the series examines the ways mythology reflects and preserves the cultures and worldviews of diverse communities across Eurasia.  In this installment, discover the mythological and spiritual traditions of the Altai people, including Ülgen, Erlik, Ak Ana, Mergen, and Bai Ulgan. The lecture explores shamanism and the dualism of Altai cosmogony, examining the powerful beings and opposing forces that shape the Altai understanding of the universe. The program concludes with a live performance of the Altai folk song Kai Kozhon.  Each program begins with a presentation by Dr. Golshat Safiullina exploring an aspect of the featured culture's mythological traditions, followed by Folk Song Club, an interactive musical experience curated by musical director Daryana Antipova, bringing another dimension to the stories, beliefs, and cultural heritage explored in the lecture.  This event is held in collaboration with the Slavic and East European Languages Department, the Jacobs School of Music, and the CHAKCHAK: Languages and Cultures Foundation.Parking Information:  Limited complimentary parking is available in front of the Museum entrance (https://maps.app.goo.gl/k4Txsojst2gSW5fUA) off Indiana Avenue. Free street parking is available in surrounding neighborhoods on weekends and weekdays after 5:00 PM.  Paid parking is also available in the University Collections at McCalla (https://maps.app.goo.gl/3i62KNcjDeCACruHA) parking lot off Indiana Avenue and the Indiana Memorial Union (https://maps.app.goo.gl/2n49VoLuF78o5twJA) visitor lot.  Metered street parking is available near Sample Gates and throughout downtown Bloomington, including along Kirkwood Avenue, East 6th Street, East 4th Street, North Lincoln Street, North Dunn Street, and South Grant Street.Questions?  For accessibility assistance or questions about this event, please reach out to Camden Hill at camrhill@iu.edu (mailto:camrhill@iu.edu) or (812) 855-1696.Note:  By attending this event, you agree to be in photography that may be used by the University for promotional purposes. If you would not like to be in any pictures, please speak to a Museum staff member and they will inform assigned photographers of your request. If you see that your image has been used in error, please reach out to iumaa@iu.edu (mailto:iumaa@iu.edu) to request that it be taken down.

title: Jessie Maple Patton Day in Bloomington, Indiana
description: Will (Jessie Maple, 1981) is the one of the earliest surviving features directed by a Black American woman. The Black Film Center & Archive has been a proud steward of the film elements, and much more, since the acquisition of The Jessie Maple Collection (https://indiana.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=f603b0d14ab6059bea01fbc72&id=d44ee48512&e=9b80f7f3db) in 2005. Having undergone a 4K restoration, Will is screening for audiences around the world! Now, Jessie Maple's films are also available to watch from the comfort of your own home on Criterion Channel! Will is included as part of the Black Debutantes (https://indiana.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=f603b0d14ab6059bea01fbc72&id=2d70d816f1&e=9b80f7f3db) lineup, which is a "celebration of pioneering Black women who made an impact with their very first—and in some cases only—feature film." Twice is Nice (Jessie Maple, 1989) is also available.  If you would like to research the Jessie Maple collection, email us at bfca@iu.edu (mailto:bfca@iu.edu) to schedule an appointment.

title: Mathematics as a Medium | Exhibition
location: Fine Arts Building, 1201 East 7th Street, Bloomington, IN 47405
description: Exhibition Opening Reception: January 15, 6:30–8:30 pmExhibition Dates: January 15–March 6Symposium Dates: January 15–16  Curated by Associate Professor of Interior Design in the Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design Jiangmei Wu, the exhibition "Mathematics as a Medium" opening Friday, January 15 at Indiana University's Grunwald Gallery of Art complements a symposium January 15 and 16 convening many of the exhibitors with counterparts from across the international mathematical art community. Over three keynotes, thematic panels, and workshops, participating artists, designers, mathematicians, and scholars will explore mathematics as an active medium of creative practice and create a shared space for exchange among disciplines.  The coordinated events seek to usher in a broader understanding of the relationship between mathematics and art. Proceeding from the proposition that mathematics is a mediumsuch as paint, stone, or sound—through which artists and designers create and cultures express themselves, the exhibition and symposium are designed more broadly to redefine mathematics as a living, generative practice that shapes how we think, make, and experience the world.Visit here for more information about the exhibition. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/exhibitions/grunwald-gallery/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium.html)Visit here for the symposium schedule. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/events/special-events/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium-symposium.html)This project was supported by Indiana University's Presidential Arts and Humanities Program; the Office for Research Development, Indiana University Research; and also at Indiana University Bloomington: Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design; Department of Mathematics; and Luddy School of Informatics, Computing and Engineering Artificial Intelligence Center (LAIC).

Every Wednesday at 8PM is Comedy Attic Open Mic Night. Bloomington has one of the best local comedy scenes in the country, and it all starts with our open mic night!

Comedians that wish to participate are asked to e-mail comedyattic@gmail.com mailto:comedyattic@gmail.com . So if you plan on signing up, be sure to invite as many friends as you can. Good luck!

title: Mathematics as a Medium | Exhibition
location: Fine Arts Building, 1201 East 7th Street, Bloomington, IN 47405
description: Exhibition Opening Reception: January 15, 6:30–8:30 pmExhibition Dates: January 15–March 6Symposium Dates: January 15–16  Curated by Associate Professor of Interior Design in the Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design Jiangmei Wu, the exhibition "Mathematics as a Medium" opening Friday, January 15 at Indiana University's Grunwald Gallery of Art complements a symposium January 15 and 16 convening many of the exhibitors with counterparts from across the international mathematical art community. Over three keynotes, thematic panels, and workshops, participating artists, designers, mathematicians, and scholars will explore mathematics as an active medium of creative practice and create a shared space for exchange among disciplines.  The coordinated events seek to usher in a broader understanding of the relationship between mathematics and art. Proceeding from the proposition that mathematics is a mediumsuch as paint, stone, or sound—through which artists and designers create and cultures express themselves, the exhibition and symposium are designed more broadly to redefine mathematics as a living, generative practice that shapes how we think, make, and experience the world.Visit here for more information about the exhibition. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/exhibitions/grunwald-gallery/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium.html)Visit here for the symposium schedule. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/events/special-events/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium-symposium.html)This project was supported by Indiana University's Presidential Arts and Humanities Program; the Office for Research Development, Indiana University Research; and also at Indiana University Bloomington: Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design; Department of Mathematics; and Luddy School of Informatics, Computing and Engineering Artificial Intelligence Center (LAIC).
source: IU Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design

title: Pacifica Quartet with James Ehnes, violin
Brittany Lasch, trombone; Eunjin Bang, piano
description: Repertoire  Emily Horton: Fantasy in G Minor (2022)Ricardo Mollá: In Pursuit of Light (2025)Cait Nishimura: Golden Hour (2020)Keiko Takashima: Breeze in the Hearts, Bloom in the World (2010/23)About the Artists  A winner of the S&R Foundation Washington Award and Astral Artists National Auditions, trombonist Brittany Lasch is associate professor of music in trombone at the Indiana University Jacobs School of Music, where she has taught since 2023. Lasch has appeared as a soloist throughout the world with ensembles ranging from the U.S. Army Band "Pershing's Own" to the Queens Symphony and the Sante Fe (Argentina) Municipal Band. With playing described as "masterful" (Syracuse Post-Standard), American Record Guide recently hailed Lasch as an "excellent soloist" across a diverse range of repertoire. Lasch has been a featured guest artist at numerous festivals, including the International Trombone Festival, the International Women's Brass Conference, and the American Trombone Workshop. For six seasons, Lasch was the principal trombone of the Detroit Opera Orchestra at the Detroit Opera House. She has performed with orchestras nationwide, such as the San Francisco Symphony, the Los Angeles Philharmonic, Indianapolis Symphony, St. Louis Symphony, Detroit Symphony, and the Nashville Symphony. An active presence in the global trombone community, Lasch has recently performed at Argentina's Trombonanza and Portugal's Gravíssimo Festival. An advocate for new music, Lasch has commissioned and performed several new pieces for the trombone, including acclaimed composer Reena Esmail's major Sonata for Trombone and Piano, which is featured on her debut album, Dark Horse (available on all streaming platforms). Lasch has previously served as faculty at the College of Musical Arts at Bowling Green State University and the Boston University Tanglewood Institute. She has also been a featured teacher and performer at summer festivals, including the Sewanee Music Festival and the DC Trombone Workshop, and she has presented master classes at universities across the country and internationally.  South Korean pianist Eunjin Bang is visiting academic specialist in chamber and collaborative music at the Indiana University Jacobs School of Music. Since moving to the United States in 2007, Bang has established herself as an award-winning performer, enthusiastic collaborator, and chamber musician. She has performed globally, including in the United States, South Korea, Germany, Spain, and Canada. Her engagements include broadcasts on WCLV radio (Cleveland) and WKAR radio (Lansing), a performing Schnittke's Piano Quartet with Sibbi Bernhardsson (former member of the Pacifica Quartet), and appearing as a soloist with the IU Philharmonic Orchestra under the baton of David Effron. As a member of the Zima Piano Trio, she won first prize in the ensemble category of the New York International Music Concours and was invited to perform at Mineral Point Chamber Music Festival in Madison, Wisconsin, and at the Absolute Chamber Music Series in Lansing, Michigan. From 2023 to 2024, Bang served as a staff pianist at Stephen F. Austin State University, including a performance at the SWACDA conference in Denver, Colorado. She served as a repetiteur for Cincinnati Opera's world-premiere staging of Paul McCartney's Liverpool Oratorio as well as for Austin, Texas, chamber orchestra Density512's premiere of Thomas Yee's Eva and the Angel of Death. Bang earned a Bachelor of Music in Piano Performance from Oberlin College and Conservatory under the guidance of Haewon Song and Master of Music, Performer Diploma, Artist Diploma, and Doctor of Music in Piano Performance from the Indiana University Jacobs School of Music under the guidance of Émile Naoumoff and Arnaldo Cohen, with double minors in music theory and collaborative piano.

title: Mathematics as a Medium | Exhibition
location: Fine Arts Building, 1201 East 7th Street, Bloomington, IN 47405
description: Exhibition Opening Reception: January 15, 6:30–8:30 pmExhibition Dates: January 15–March 6Symposium Dates: January 15–16  Curated by Associate Professor of Interior Design in the Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design Jiangmei Wu, the exhibition "Mathematics as a Medium" opening Friday, January 15 at Indiana University's Grunwald Gallery of Art complements a symposium January 15 and 16 convening many of the exhibitors with counterparts from across the international mathematical art community. Over three keynotes, thematic panels, and workshops, participating artists, designers, mathematicians, and scholars will explore mathematics as an active medium of creative practice and create a shared space for exchange among disciplines.  The coordinated events seek to usher in a broader understanding of the relationship between mathematics and art. Proceeding from the proposition that mathematics is a mediumsuch as paint, stone, or sound—through which artists and designers create and cultures express themselves, the exhibition and symposium are designed more broadly to redefine mathematics as a living, generative practice that shapes how we think, make, and experience the world.Visit here for more information about the exhibition. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/exhibitions/grunwald-gallery/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium.html)Visit here for the symposium schedule. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/events/special-events/upcoming/2027-01-15-math-medium-symposium.html)This project was supported by Indiana University's Presidential Arts and Humanities Program; the Office for Research Development, Indiana University Research; and also at Indiana University Bloomington: Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design; Department of Mathematics; and Luddy School of Informatics, Computing and Engineering Artificial Intelligence Center (LAIC).
